data.narrative:
Kyoto Fusioneering is a Series C-stage nuclear energy company that has raised $125M+ to date. The valuation universe comprises 11 comparable firms across public and private markets—3 publicly traded peers (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private companies including Oklo, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, and Fuse Energy. This peer set establishes sector context but does not yield a statistically reliable same-stage cohort for direct median comparison.

Given data constraints, the analysis relies on stage-progression methodology. Using total raised ($125M) as a valuation proxy and applying a typical Series C-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 1.7x yields an implied valuation of $212M. This method is applicable where peer comps are sparse and represents the primary quantitative anchor in the absence of sufficient narrow-cohort comparables.

The triangulated valuation range is $181M–$244M, centered on a median of $212M. This range reflects uncertainty inherent in single-method triangulation. Key unknowns include (1) the absence of same-stage nuclear peers with disclosed valuations sufficient to calibrate multiple-based approaches, (2) the appropriateness of the 1.7x multiplier to Kyoto Fusioneering's specific capital efficiency and technical progress, and (3) sector-wide valuation volatility in early-stage nuclear. A more granular range would require either additional disclosed comparable transactions or clearer visibility into revenue trajectory and technical milestones.
